name: Carlos Ramirez-Rosa
interest: Sits at the center of the CPD administrative decision chain; can direct departments to establish a defined administrative status and refer any Board action needed.
infoNeeded: Problem statement, evidence summary, precedent set, departmental findings, community support, exact decision requested.
infoNotNeeded: Full 40-slide evidence bank; raw FOIA drafts; internal department disagreements.
ask: Direct the relevant CPD departments to establish a defined administrative status for the 63rd Street Beach complex enabling dedicated PAC representation, and refer any required action to the Board.
approachedBy: LCA liaison / Alderman's office (introduction), then direct executive briefing.
followUp: Written response to the six Gate 0 determination questions (see Global Master Presentation).

name: Board of Commissioners (7 members)
department: Governing Board — management & control of CPD business and property
interest: Any classification, policy amendment, or land/park-designation action ultimately requiring Board approval needs 4 of 7 affirmative votes.
infoNeeded: Concise decision brief + evidence appendix; legal memo from Law; Superintendent's recommendation.
infoNotNeeded: Constituent-level community stories in full; internal CPD departmental process detail.
ask: Approve whichever Board action Law/the Superintendent determine is required (park/administrative-unit designation, policy amendment, or acknowledgment of staff determination).
approachedBy: General Superintendent's office, after Gate 0 pathway is confirmed; Board President's office for agenda placement.
followUp: Board resolution or meeting-minute record of the vote.

name: Programs & Recreation Committee
department: Board Committee — jurisdiction over community/advisory-council relations, naming, recreation & cultural matters
interest: Likely first committee stop for the community-representation and PAC-recognition dimension of the request.
infoNeeded: Why distinct community representation is warranted; BBPAC scope and readiness.
infoNotNeeded: Property/boundary legal detail (belongs to Capital Improvements).
ask: Recommend the full Board consider the recognition request favorably.
approachedBy: Board Secretary's office, per standing-committee referral (unless suspended by the Board President).
presentationLabel: Board of Commissioners Decision Brief (Programs & Recreation module)

name: Capital Improvements Committee
department: Board Committee — jurisdiction over long-term facility plans, land sale/lease/transfer/acquisition
interest: Owns the boundary / park-identity / property-classification dimension of the request.
infoNeeded: Park #19 boundary facts, precedent set (Maggie Daley, Seneca, Rutherford Sayre, Lane Beach), proposed BBPAC jurisdiction map.
ask: Confirm the property/classification mechanism proposed is sound and recommend Board approval if a land or classification action is required.
approachedBy: Board Secretary's office, per standing-committee referral.
presentationLabel: Board of Commissioners Decision Brief (Capital Improvements module)

name: Administration Committee
department: Board Committee — legal matters, government relations, general policy
interest: Owns the legal-authority / policy-amendment dimension if current PAC policy must change.
infoNeeded: Law Department's memo on authority and required instrument.
ask: Recommend any necessary policy amendment to the full Board.
approachedBy: Board Secretary's office, per standing-committee referral.
presentationLabel: Board of Commissioners Decision Brief (Administration module)

name: Alderman Desmon Yancy
interest: 63rd Street Beach is a historic 5th Ward lakefront asset; representation, investment, safety and accountability all matter directly to his constituents.
infoNeeded: Community representation case, historical stewardship, investment case, public safety, cultural preservation, accountability gap.
infoNotNeeded: Deep CPD internal-classification statutory citations (Law/Planning's job, not his).
ask: Become the governmental sponsor/champion of the BBPAC recognition initiative and formally request an interdepartmental CPD determination.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, directly, early in the campaign.
followUp: Sponsorship letter to CPD leadership; ward-office constituent-support tracking.

name: Mayor's Office
department: Office of the Mayor / Intergovernmental Affairs
interest: Appoints all 7 Park District Board members (with City Council approval); becomes important if the campaign hits institutional resistance or a significant policy question.
infoNeeded: High-level summary only — problem, ask, current status. Not a Gate 0 audience.
ask: Awareness now; escalation support later if CPD leadership does not act on a reasonable timeline.
approachedBy: Alderman Yancy's office, if/when escalation is needed.
presentationLabel: Mayor's Office / City Council Committee Briefing
followUp: None at this stage — held in reserve.
status: Not started — held for escalation lane

name: Special Events, Cultural Affairs & Recreation Committee
department: City Council Committee — jurisdiction over park-system and CPD-affecting matters
interest: Oversight/political forum if the issue requires City involvement, legislation, hearings, or public pressure. Does not itself approve CPD's internal classification.
infoNeeded: High-level summary; used only if escalation is required.
ask: None at Gate 0 — held in reserve as an oversight/pressure valve.
approachedBy: Alderman Yancy's office, if escalation is needed.
presentationLabel: Mayor's Office / City Council Committee Briefing
status: Not started — held for escalation lane

name: Ismael Cuevas
interest: LCA is the PAC gatekeeper and process owner — responsible for working with communities to create PACs and liaising with PACs, alderpersons and government bodies.
infoNeeded: The PAC problem, the one-PAC-per-park rule, proposed BBPAC structure, community need, the classification issue.
ask: Identify the official pathway by which BBPAC can become eligible and recognized, and coordinate the internal CPD review.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee — first internal CPD contact per published PAC rules.
followUp: Written pathway determination; internal review coordination record.

name: Heather Gleason
interest: Manages land acquisition, property inventory, historic analysis, park research/policy and development plans — the most important technical department for this request.
infoNeeded: Historical maps, Park #19 boundaries, Lane Beach #1265, Seneca #1242, Maggie Daley, Rutherford Sayre, South Park history, proposed BBPAC boundary.
infoNotNeeded: Community petition signatures; cultural programming detail.
ask: Determine and document the administrative/property mechanism for establishing a distinct park unit and boundary.
approachedBy: LCA, after initial intake, or directly alongside LCA.
followUp: Written technical determination on classification mechanism.

name: Heather L. Keil
interest: Determines what CPD legally can do and what instrument (staff determination, Superintendent action, Board resolution, or policy amendment) is required.
infoNeeded: A concise legal/precedent memo request — not the full community deck.
infoNotNeeded: Community narrative, cultural/historical detail beyond what's legally relevant.
ask: What authority permits this? What action is required? Is Board approval necessary? Does a separate park number require a land action, classification action, or administrative record change?
approachedBy: LCA / Planning, after initial intake, or by direct referral from the Superintendent's office.
followUp: Written legal opinion on required instrument and authority.

name: Patrick J. Levar
interest: Executive integrator across Planning & Development, Facility Management, Environmental Services, Natural Resources and Security.
infoNeeded: Operational case for why the beach already functions as a specialized complex distinct from ordinary Jackson Park operations.
infoNotNeeded: Legal statutory citations; community petition detail.
ask: Is a distinct administrative unit operationally viable, and will Operations support the recommendation?
approachedBy: LCA / Superintendent's office, mid-process.

name: James Sifuentes
interest: Ground-level park administration; South Region already lists Jackson Park among its major properties.
infoNeeded: Existing operations, staffing, programming, community use, and proposed division of responsibilities between BBPAC and JPAC scope.
ask: Operational assessment and cooperation — not the classification decision itself.
approachedBy: COO's office or directly by BBPAC organizing committee for a fact-finding conversation.

name: Bobbie Beckam
interest: CPD's own PAC rules direct citizens to start with the Park Supervisor or Area Manager.
infoNeeded: Short factual presentation: existing conditions, representation gap, proposed boundaries.
infoNotNeeded: Full precedent library, legal memos — outside this role's authority.
ask: Document current operations and elevate the request; this office does not decide what it lacks authority to decide.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee — often the very first conversation.
followUp: Elevation of request to LCA/Area Manager chain.

name: Natural Resources / Lakefront Operations
interest: Beaches, natural areas, water quality, dunes and ecological management make the 63rd Street site operationally distinct.
infoNeeded: Dune/shoreline habitat data, water-quality and stewardship module.
ask: Technical validation of the site's distinct environmental stewardship responsibilities.
approachedBy: COO's office or Planning, as a technical-validation step.

name: Aquatics
interest: Manages the lakefront swimming-beach program (lifeguards, swim safety, seasonality).
infoNeeded: Beach use, lifeguard staffing, swimming access, seasonal operations.
ask: Technical statement confirming specialized beach operations distinct from inland park recreation.
approachedBy: Operations/COO chain, as a technical-validation step.

name: Facility Management
interest: Beach House building condition, maintenance history, and capital needs.
infoNeeded: Beach House condition/history/capital section of the case.
ask: Confirm facility-management realities and capital needs referenced in the case.
approachedBy: COO's office / Planning, as a technical-validation step.

name: Revenue
interest: 63rd Street Beach House is already a CPD-designated special-event venue; Revenue coordinates special-event permitting.
infoNeeded: Rentals, events, concessions, and commercial-activity detail.
ask: Document that the Beach House already has functions distinct from ordinary Jackson Park recreation.
approachedBy: COO's office, as a technical-validation step.

name: Park Public Safety
interest: Security and coordination with police/emergency agencies for the beach and Beach House.
infoNeeded: Public-safety and event-safety portion of the case only.
ask: Validate the specialized public-safety environment of a major open-water swimming beach and special-event venue.
approachedBy: COO's office, as a technical-validation step.
presentationLabel: Operations & Community Recreation Deck (Public Safety module)

name: Budget & Management
interest: Becomes important once an administrative structure is contemplated — staffing/cost-center/capital implications.
infoNeeded: Fiscal-impact summary tied to whichever administrative option is recommended.
ask: Determine whether separate administrative recognition has material fiscal consequences.
approachedBy: Superintendent's office, once a preferred option is identified.

name: Communications
interest: Not an initial decision-maker; owns public rollout only after a path has been established.
infoNeeded: The final, approved narrative — nothing before that.
infoNotNeeded: Internal deliberation, unresolved evidence, draft precedent arguments.
ask: None at Gate 0 — engage last, for public rollout only.
approachedBy: Superintendent's office, after a decision is reached.
presentationLabel: No dedicated deck — engage after a decision is reached

name: Jackson Park Advisory Council (JPAC)
department: Existing Park Advisory Council for Park #19
interest: Currently the registered PAC for all of Jackson Park, including 63rd Street Beach; publicly represents all Jackson Park users.
infoNeeded: What BBPAC would represent, what JPAC continues to represent, what remains shared, and how the two councils would coordinate. Framed as 'Two Strong Voices, One Historic Jackson Park Landscape' — never as a failure narrative.
infoNotNeeded: A neglect/blame narrative directed at JPAC — this is deliberately excluded from their presentation.
ask: Support, or at minimum neutrality/no objection to BBPAC recognition, or a documented opportunity to comment. Never framed as required consent unless CPD says otherwise.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, directly and respectfully, early enough to avoid the appearance of end-running them.
followUp: Documented position (support / neutral / comment) for the record.

name: South Shore Cultural Center Advisory Council
organization: South Shore Cultural Center Advisory Council
interest: Not a parcel-split precedent, but the strongest working example of a dedicated, specialized lakefront-site PAC succeeding at cultural programming, fundraising and preservation advocacy.
infoNeeded: Comparative case-study framing: what a dedicated lakefront PAC can accomplish.
infoNotNeeded: Jackson Park boundary/classification detail — not their issue.
ask: Will you share your institutional experience and, if appropriate, support the proposition that specialized South Side lakefront assets benefit from dedicated community advisory representation?
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, as a peer-to-peer outreach.
followUp: Letter of support or shared-experience testimonial.

name: Friends of the Parks
interest: Actively supports and describes Chicago PACs as neighborhood-led community voices; carries independent parks-policy credibility.
infoNeeded: Governance/precedent case for dedicated representation of specialized lakefront assets.
ask: Endorse the governance case and lend independent parks-policy credibility to the campaign.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, once the Global Master case is stable.

name: Chicago Parks Foundation
department: Fiscal sponsor for PACs and park partners
interest: Relevant to what BBPAC becomes after recognition (fiscal sponsorship), not to whether Park #19 should be reconfigured. Not asked to solve Gate 0.
infoNeeded: Post-recognition BBPAC structure and fundraising needs.
ask: Explore a future fiscal-sponsorship relationship once BBPAC is formally recognized and formed.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, deliberately held until after Gate 0.
status: Not started — held for post-recognition phase

name: Bongo / drumming community
interest: Protection of cultural history, continued access, and recognized cultural programming at Bongo Beach.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation and FAQ.
infoNotNeeded: Statutory citations, GIS boundary data, internal CPD org charts.
ask: Sign the community-support petition; attend public meetings; share your history and connection to the site.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.

name: Beach users & families
interest: Restrooms, cleanliness, access, safety, parking and facilities.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation and FAQ.
ask: Sign the community-support petition; share direct experience of current conditions.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.

name: Swimmers
interest: Lifeguards, water quality, and swimming access.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation and FAQ.
ask: Sign the community-support petition.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.

name: Environmental community
interest: Dunes, habitat, and shoreline stewardship — roughly 12 acres of native dune/shoreline habitat.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation, plus the environmental-stewardship module of the Global deck.
ask: Sign the community-support petition; consider a formal organizational endorsement.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.
followUp: Signed petition entry; possible organizational endorsement.

name: Historic-preservation community
interest: Beach House preservation (built 1919) and capital investment.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation, plus the historical/cultural module of the Global deck.
ask: Sign the community-support petition; consider a formal organizational endorsement.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.
followUp: Signed petition entry; possible organizational endorsement.

name: Youth, parents & schools
interest: Programming, leadership opportunities, and safe recreation.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation and FAQ.
ask: Sign the community-support petition; attend public meetings.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.

name: Seniors & disability advocates
interest: ADA access and usable facilities.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation and FAQ.
ask: Sign the community-support petition; share accessibility concerns for the Conditions & Neglect Dossier.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.

name: Event / community organizers
interest: Fair access, transparent permitting, and cultural programming opportunities.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation and FAQ.
ask: Sign the community-support petition; consider becoming a founding BBPAC member.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.

name: Neighbors
interest: Accountability and a direct community voice in how the beach is managed.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation and FAQ.
ask: Sign the community-support petition.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.

name: Businesses & institutions
interest: Partnerships, visitor activity, and responsible activation of the site.
infoNeeded: The plain-language community presentation and FAQ.
ask: Sign the community-support petition; consider organizational endorsement or sponsorship interest.
approachedBy: BBPAC organizing committee, community outreach lane.
